predeclared_hypotheses: All five byte-identical v1.0.2 model inputs reproduce the same typed assignment: two TEACH-AIR-01 on SUPPORT, one EXEC-AIR-01 on EXECUTE, one ready support spare. Exact 17/18 populated source business tables roundtrip, conversion has zero errors and only logging/no-items warnings.

Each run has the same SUPPORT critical failure and 0.5-hour suspension, with a prepared TEACH-AIR-01 replacement, and the same EXECUTE no-failure clock. If SUPPORT failure identity or gap timing differs across variants, the tolerance contrast is NO-GO.
With no dependency, EXECUTE stays operating through the SUPPORT gap and succeeds at scheduled hour 11.9; SUPPORT succeeds at hour 12.
With DTTOL=0, EXECUTE suspends at SUPPORT gap onset and resumes when SUPPORT resumes, with 0.5 hour of dependent suspended exposure; it is not predicted to abort.
With DTTOL=0.49, EXECUTE suspends at gap onset plus 0.49 hours and resumes at gap end, with approximately 0.01 hour of dependent suspended exposure.

With DTTOL=0.5, an event at the exact gap end may record a same-time suspend/resume but yields zero duration of dependent suspended exposure. With DTTOL=0.51, no gap-related EXECUTE suspension occurs.

All five EXECUTE missions succeed at hour 11.9 and all SUPPORT missions succeed at hour 12. Full event identities, preparation/failure/repair ledgers, 32 half-hour System/Stock bins, summary factors and terminal four-ready state must reconcile.
A separate reviewer must replay the source and raw evidence without importing the author validator. Any failed hypothesis remains diagnostic rather than silently accepted.
limits: This is a reproducibility check of one fixed-seed stochastic half-hour SUPPORT gap in one explicit unit, not a general DTTOL law or deterministic failure schedule.
DTTOL effects with absent predecessor, longer gap, multiple precedents, other mission patterns, cross-unit/profile dependence, GUI visual content and cross-engine equivalence remain unverified.
